scope: The late nineteenth-century blacksmith forge at the Obadjiwan trading post, with its full measured timber enclosure, steep gable roof, little west door canopy, single adjacent window and masonry stack at the south gable.
era: Late Hudson’s Bay Company trading post, represented in 1888.

stories.title: Fort Temiscamingue: Where the Cedars Dance at the Narrows

originalReview.notes: A wide shore view of the HBC-era building group. The distant photograph establishes exterior massing and relative landscape. Individual facade details require measured or written evidence.

review.method: Qualla native original and primary archival rights
review.notes: Reviewed the original Qualla set first. The exact 1876 McLaughlin waterfront photograph has native public-domain tags and an item-specific expiry record. It supports the overall late nineteenth-century timber post appearance. The specific forge elevations and measured plan follow the excavation report.
